analysis.title: US Midterm Elections Outcome (Fundamental Flash)
key_insights: Democrats swept both chambers of Congress per AP as of 6 November 2026: Senate 54 seats (+7), Republicans 44, and House 253 (+41) vs Republicans 157. Divided government begins January 2027.

AHAM attributes the result to voter dissatisfaction with the Iran war and rising living costs. VP Vance acknowledged the war's role, framing the outcome as a rebuke of the administration's record rather than an endorsement of the Democratic agenda.
Trump will find it harder to advance tax and spending measures without bipartisan support. A Democratic Senate becomes gatekeeper for judicial and senior government appointments.

Gridlock constrains both sides: Democrats lack the 60 Senate votes needed for most legislation and the two-thirds majorities needed to override a veto. AHAM expects the White House to rely more on executive action and foreign policy, and says policy uncertainty will persist.

Initial market optimism over gridlock gave way to concerns that the election outcome could slow AI infrastructure investment. Data centres became a campaign issue over electricity bills, water consumption and limited permanent job creation.

Combined capex at Meta, Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon reached about USD 202 billion in Q3 2026, while their combined free cash flow turned negative at about USD 26 billion. This sharpens questions about how further expansion is funded and when it earns sufficient returns.

US leveraged ETFs drew about USD 15 billion in October, the largest monthly inflow in at least two years (industry estimates), as investors bought the dip before the election. Leverage amplified the selling when sentiment reversed.

AHAM views a broad US AI ban as unlikely given the strategic need to compete with China. The nearer risk is tighter state-level regulation that could slow data centre development, particularly after Democratic wins in Texas and Ohio.

Requirements for operators to secure their own power and protect households from higher electricity bills could raise costs and delay some projects. Over time these safeguards could rebuild public trust and support a more sustainable buildout.

Positioning: AHAM cut technology hardware exposure before the election over AI revenue growth and capex funding concerns, trimmed further since, and remains underweight pending clarity on state-level data centre policy and hyperscaler funding.

sector_views.rationale: Concerns over AI revenue growth and funding of further capex, plus uncertainty over state-level data centre policy and hyperscaler funding.

risk_factors: Tighter state-level data centre regulation could slow AI infrastructure buildout and raise costs for operators

Policy uncertainty persists under divided government, with the White House likely to lean on executive action
